description: Voice IDs for paired battle operation callouts (normal, onslaught/aggressive, cooperation and caution) and the teammate's answer voice, keyed by character-operation row.

Id.simple: Character-operation row key; most rows are keyed by a character ID, but several character rows deliberately share one operation row.
Id.technical: FName Id is the reflected struct field (serialized as ID in the export); the DataTable row name is the key passed to FindRow. AGameCharacter::ResolveDataRows reads CharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterOperation without an override, finds the first match in CharacterOperationDataTables (DTM +0x540), and caches it at OperationRow (+0x3D8); a miss fails character setup. All 27 exported row names equal their Id field.

Id_Voice_Normal.technical: FName Id_Voice_Normal. When Kind is not 2/3/4 (including the producer's Kind 1), Tick reads it from the speaker's cached operation row, shows BTL_HUD_LABEL_0201 ("Normal" in the English text export), and calls PlayVoiceById with Speaker->GetCharacterIndex().

Id_Voice_Receive_Normal.simple: Partner's reply to a normal callout.
Id_Voice_Receive_Normal.technical: FName Id_Voice_Receive_Normal. The default-kind responder key is copied from the responder's cached row. It plays only after the speaker handle is no longer playing, the responder passes CanAnswerExchangeVoice, and Timer reaches 0.5 s; the playback slot is Responder->GetCharacterIndex().

Id_Voice_Onslaught.technical: FName Id_Voice_Onslaught. Kind 2 selects this speaker key and BTL_HUD_LABEL_0202 ("Aggressive" in the English text export); PlayVoiceById uses the speaker's character index.

Id_Voice_Receive_Onslaught.simple: Partner's reply to an onslaught/aggressive callout.
Id_Voice_Receive_Onslaught.technical: FName Id_Voice_Receive_Onslaught. Kind 2 copies this responder key from the responder's cached row; after the speaker clip ends and CanAnswerExchangeVoice succeeds, the 0.5 s timer gates playback on the responder's character index.

Id_Voice_Cooperation.technical: FName Id_Voice_Cooperation. Kind 3 selects this speaker key and BTL_HUD_LABEL_0203 ("Cooperative" in the English text export); PlayVoiceById uses the speaker's character index.

Id_Voice_Receive_Cooperation.simple: Partner's reply to a cooperation callout.
Id_Voice_Receive_Cooperation.technical: FName Id_Voice_Receive_Cooperation. Kind 3 pairs this responder key with Id_Voice_Cooperation and holds it in ResponderVoice for the delayed answer playback on the responder's character index.

Id_Voice_Carefully.technical: FName Id_Voice_Carefully. Kind 4 selects this speaker key and BTL_HUD_LABEL_0204 ("Cautious" in the English text export); PlayVoiceById uses the speaker's character index.

Id_Voice_Receive_Carefully.simple: Partner's reply to a careful/cautious callout.
Id_Voice_Receive_Carefully.technical: FName Id_Voice_Receive_Carefully. Kind 4 pairs this responder key with Id_Voice_Carefully; after the speaker clip ends and CanAnswerExchangeVoice succeeds, it is played after the 0.5 s timer on the responder's character index.

notes: Kind comes from FStudioBattleVoiceExchange.Kind, queued by AGameBattleManager::AddVoiceExchange from the released operation direction (Kinds 1-4). FStudioBattleSystem320::Tick maps 2/3/4 to BTL_HUD_LABEL_0202/0203/0204 and every other value, including Kind 1 and the struct default 0, to BTL_HUD_LABEL_0201. The English BattleTextDataTable labels those four messages Normal, Aggressive, Cooperative and Cautious.

One primary asset named CharacterOperationDataTable is resolved into DTM.CharacterOperationDataTables (+0x540). ResolveDataRows caches the first FindRow match in AGameCharacter.OperationRow (+0x3D8), and no operation-id override is applied; the only direct field reads in the available source are in FStudioBattleSystem320::Tick, while the controller and battle manager pass weak speaker/responder references plus Kind.

Exchange state: Step 0 discards the exchange if the speaker cannot speak or an operation message is already opening; otherwise it selects the speaker/responder voice pair, shows the HUD message and plays the speaker voice. Step 1 waits until that handle is no longer playing, then requires CanAnswerExchangeVoice; Step 2 accumulates DeltaTime in seconds until >= 0.5 before playing the reply; Step 3 discards the exchange when the reply stops. No distance, range or volume value is stored in this table.

PlayVoiceById resolves each FName against DTM.VoiceDataTables with GameScript_FindVoiceRow(..., bCheckNone=true, bUnknown=false); a missing Voice row returns handle -1. IsVoicePlaying(-1) is false, so a missing speaker key lets the state advance immediately after the responder check, while a missing responder key is discarded on the next tick. VoiceDataTable supplies CueSheetName/CueName, and PlayVoice appends "_En" to the cue at runtime when bAppendEnVoiceSuffix is set.

Export content: one unsharded, unlocalized table with 27 rows. Every row name equals its Id, all eight voice FNames are non-None and resolve to VoiceDataTable rows, and in every row the four receive fields are the same key (VoCha_<row>_08_2_010); the speaker fields use the _15_, _44_, _21_ and _45_ suffixes. Those numeric suffixes are observed data, not documented semantics.

CharacterData relationship: 47 of its 48 exported rows reference one of these 27 rows; CN_210 uses the FName None sentinel and would fail the non-optional operation lookup if set up. Sharing is intentional: 19 character rows point at CP_010, CP_081 at CP_080, and CN_260 at CP_160.

No localized variants of this table were exported; downstream BattleTextDataTable carries localized labels, and voice cue names are localized at playback. The 27 exported rows are the available content only: no claim is made about additional retail rows or Blueprint-only consumers.
Evidence is reconstructed C++ with retail RVAs recorded in source; it establishes the reconstructed runtime behavior but is not a retail byte-match claim. No retail Blueprint evidence was available.

usages.detail: Resolves the single CharacterOperationDataTable primary asset into CharacterOperationDataTables (DTM +0x540).
Resolves the row by CharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterOperation with no override and caches it in AGameCharacter.OperationRow (+0x3D8); a miss fails setup.
Queues an exchange with the player as speaker, the selected ally as responder, and the released direction as Kind 1-4.
Stores the speaker, responder and Kind in a System320.Exchanges entry.
Selects the speaker/receiver voice pair from both cached CharacterOperation rows by exchange kind and labels the HUD operation message.
Plays the selected speaker voice with the speaker's character index.
Gates the reply on the speaker playback ending, the responder being able to answer, and the 0.5 s timer.
Plays the selected reply voice with the responder's character index.
Resolves the FName through VoiceDataTables and turns its row into CRI Atom cue sheet/cue playback; returns -1 for a missing row.
Appends the runtime English cue suffix when configured; this is downstream of the operation-to-voice lookup.
